title: Frijoles Charros (Rancho Gordo Pinto & Mayocoba)
headnote: DRAFT / TESTED WITH PROBLEMS. Adapted from Serious Eats in September 2026. Final discussed batch changed from all-pinto to 225 g Rancho Gordo pinto plus 225 g mayocoba beans, with chicken stock and a bacon-tomato base. User reported a difficult trial: pintos mostly tender after about 5½ hours, mayocobas still firm, and baking soda caused rapid thickening/sticking. This is not a confirmed successful final recipe.

ingredientGroups.title: Bean pot
items: 225 g dried Rancho Gordo pinto beans
18 g salt for the original soak (if soaking; drain afterward)
Approximately 1,400 g unsalted chicken stock (original: 6 cups); add just enough to cover the beans and top up as needed
6 g kosher salt to begin cooking (from September 8 adjustment); adjust at end

steps: Sort and rinse the beans. If using the original salted soak, dissolve the 18 g salt in sufficient water, soak the beans, then drain and rinse before cooking.

Place the beans in a heavy pot and add enough unsalted chicken stock to just cover (up to approximately 1.4 kg initially), topping up during cooking as needed. Add the initial 6 g salt; reserve final seasoning until tender.

Simmer gently until both bean varieties are truly tender, checking frequently and adding stock as necessary. Do not rely on a fixed time: in the user's trial, pintos were mostly tender after about 5½ hours but mayocobas were still firm.
Separately, cook the chopped bacon until rendered; soften the onion and serrano in the fat, then add garlic and fire-roasted tomatoes. Cook until the base is fragrant and slightly reduced.

When beans are tender, stir the bacon-tomato mixture into the pot and simmer another 20–30 minutes to meld, or combine cooked beans and base approximately 1:1 by weight when assembling smaller portions. This reflects the September 15 final discussion.
Taste and adjust salt and thickness. Do not use baking soda to force completion: during the earlier trial it caused the liquid to thicken rapidly and stick.
reviewFlags: DRAFT / TESTED WITH PROBLEMS — not a verified successful recipe.
The user's actual mixed-bean test required ~5½ hours for mostly tender pintos, while mayocobas were still firm.
Baking soda caused thickening and sticking; the final draft avoids it.
Earlier all-pinto version used 450 g pinto beans; latest proposed batch was 225 g pinto + 225 g mayocoba. Both are preserved in notes, with the latest in ingredients.
The Fat Duck pressure-cooker stock process was discussed but full stock instructions were not recovered; this draft uses prepared unsalted chicken stock.
